r4-quality.finding:
Per-rule check against the 5 protected-intent items: (1) no-engine-logic-duplicated -- engine diff empty, every branch in call_tool() routes through run_engine()->checklist_engine.main(), confirmed by reading all of mcp_spine_server.py. (2) imperative-verbatim -- as_result() returns (stdout+stderr).strip() verbatim; independently reproduced the negative control (see r3-evidence). Minor nuance for Workflow Feedback: both sides are compared after .strip(), so the proven claim is 'identical after whitespace-trim', a hair narrower than literal 'byte-identical', though substantively the same guarantee since both the CLI capture and the tool result apply the same normalization. (3) CLI-door-stays -- verified by direct enumeration against usage: checklist_engine.py [-h] --file FILE [--dry-run]
                           {current,claim,heartbeat,release,start,advance,record,consolidate,skip,block,resume,reopen,append,amend,attest,waive,attach,flag-candidate}
                           ...

Workbench checklist engine: work one gated/survey plan through its gates. The
engine holds the canonical state; an agent transacts with it one step at a
time. It enforces *mechanism* (ordering, evidence shape, the rework cap, the
consolidation consistency guard) and never judges quality. See
docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md.

positional arguments:
  {current,claim,heartbeat,release,start,advance,record,consolidate,skip,block,resume,reopen,append,amend,attest,waive,attach,flag-candidate}

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --file FILE           checklist JSON file
  --dry-run             do not write changes back: 18 verbs total (current, claim, heartbeat, release, start, advance, record, consolidate, skip, block, resume, reopen, append, amend, attest, waive, attach, flag-candidate); 13 covered by the 7 tools (current/claim/heartbeat/release/start/advance/attest/attach/waive/block/resume/record/consolidate), 5 uncovered (skip/reopen/append/amend/flag-candidate) all documented in the module docstring's CLI-fallback table with invocation shape + rationale; 13+5=18, disjoint, matches claim exactly. (4) settings.json never written -- grepped scripts/mcp_spine_server.py, scripts/gen_mcp_config.py, .mcp.json, tests/test_mcp_spine_server.py: zero hits. (5) each agent own server instance -- SPINE_FILE/SPINE_ENGINE/SPINE_SESSION are bound at module-import time from env (mcp_spine_server.py lines 112-114), so one OS process = one dedicated identity; gen_mcp_config.py composes SPINE_SESSION as session_id#agent_id per dispatch. CREW_CONTEXT.md verification-discipline rules also checked: guard loops (CliFallbackTableTests) assert per-item via assertIn in a real loop and a real set-intersection, not a vacuous pass.

r6-fowler.title: Refactoring pass (Fowler code smells)
r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards — an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json, run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py <record> (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. This item's postcondition command ships with a <fowler-pass-record-path> placeholder; record() runs that command and refuses `pass` while it fails. NORMAL PATH -- resolve the placeholder to the real record path when you INSTANTIATE this survey from the template, before you claim: it is an instantiation-time substitution exactly like <work-id> on line 2. That is the documented route and the one you should be on. REPAIR PATH -- only if the record later moves or the path you substituted was wrong, correct it through the engine with `amend --delta <file>` whose single op is `retext-check` on this item's c1, never by hand-editing this survey. There, --authority is the dispatching Commander named in your reviewer handoff (never a string you invent), and --reason is why the path changed. Do NOT silently skip this item.

r7-delivery-path.title: Delivery-path decision: re-verify, do not inherit
r7-delivery-path.imperative: Re-run the Commander's project-scope .mcp.json probe independently. Answer whether Pending approval is a PERMANENT state for a cold/headless agent, or a ONE-TIME first-use state that clears once approved. If project-scope .mcp.json would serve a headless agent fine (one-time or otherwise), the per-dispatch config-generation architecture is aimed at the wrong problem -- BLOCK.
r7-delivery-path.finding:
BLOCK. Re-ran the probe independently, on Claude Code 2.1.226 (claude --version), against the worktree's own committed project-scope .mcp.json, in a project directory with ZERO prior state (no entry at all for /home/tommy/projects/constellation-skills-wt/f-424 in ~/.claude.json before this review -- a genuinely cold project, not a re-used one).

Step 1 -- confirmed the interactive-mode status the Commander cited: `claude mcp list` / `claude mcp get spine` show "spine: python3 scripts/mcp_spine_server.py - Pending approval (run `claude` to approve)".

Step 2 -- tested whether that blocks a real headless dispatch (the actual question this gate turns on): `claude -p "Call the mcp tool spine__spine_status..." --output-format json --allowedTools "mcp__spine__spine_status"`, no --mcp-config, no --strict-mcp-config, plain ambient project .mcp.json. Result: is_error=false, and the tool returned genuine engine output naming the interactive-demo spine's real active gate. Verified this was NOT a hallucinated transcript by checking server-side ground truth independent of the model's claim: .agent-work/.../interactive-demo/mcp_calls.jsonl grew from 2 to 3 lines with a fresh matching timestamp, and mcp_server_started already existed -- the server process genuinely launched and a real checklist_engine.main(["current"]) call ran. Repeated a second time: line count grew 2->3 again, same result. ~/.claude.json still shows no entry for this project after both calls -- no approval was ever recorded or required.

Step 3 -- isolated WHY the Commander's original probe likely saw a block: re-ran the identical -p call WITHOUT --allowedTools. Result: permission_denials=[{"tool_name": "mcp__spine__spine_status", ...}], and the model's own text says "The tool exists but I don't have permission to call it." This is the ORDINARY per-tool-call permission gate every tool (Bash, Edit, any MCP tool) has in headless mode absent an explicit grant -- NOT the MCP-server "Pending approval" connection gate. The two are different mechanisms. gen_mcp_config.py's own proof-of-delivery in the implementer's evidence ALSO passes --allowedTools "mcp__spine__spine_status" -- so this friction is identical whether the door is reached via plain project .mcp.json or via per-dispatch --mcp-config/--strict-mcp-config. Per-dispatch config generation buys nothing against this gate that plain .mcp.json + --allowedTools does not already have.

Answer to the handoff's question: "Pending approval" is not permanent for a cold/headless agent, and it is not even a one-time-clearing state that needs a single interactive approval first -- headless `-p` dispatch does not appear to hit that gate at all in this Claude Code version. Project-scope .mcp.json serves a headless agent today, out of the box, with the same --allowedTools requirement any tool call needs. The premise stated in MISSION_FRAME.md ("project-scope .mcp.json ... cannot serve a cold agent at all") and repeated in the g1-implementer-handoff and execute.json's decision:mcp-probe-is-the-commanders (graded settled/measured) is empirically wrong as measured here, on this host, this CLI version, right now (per doctrine: pin the claim to the revision read).

This does not necessarily mean gen_mcp_config.py should be deleted -- protected-intent item 5 (each agent gets its OWN server instance, keyed session_id#agentId) is a real, independent requirement a single shared project .mcp.json cannot satisfy on its own, because SPINE_FILE/SPINE_SESSION are bound once at server-launch from one static .mcp.json entry, so N concurrently-dispatched agents sharing that one project config would all bind the SAME spine file and SESSION identity. That is a genuine, different justification for per-dispatch config generation -- but it is not the justification MISSION_FRAME and the implementer handoff actually recorded, and Commander built and graded a decision (settled/measured) on a measurement that does not reproduce. Per @grade doctrine, settled/measured is revisable by a contradicting new measurement -- this is that measurement, logged here as the new provenance. This is a genuine BLOCK per the handoff's own stated close criterion, not a nice-to-have: "If it is one-time ... the delivery architecture is aimed at the wrong problem and that is a BLOCK" -- my finding is the stronger case of that same condition (not even one-time-gated).

Scoped null: tested on Claude Code 2.1.226, Linux host, this specific .mcp.json shape (one server, one tool named in --allowedTools), print-mode (-p) with --output-format json. NOT tested: other CLI versions, --dangerously-skip-permissions, or genuinely concurrent multi-agent dispatch racing the same project .mcp.json (which is where the real, different justification above would need its own re-verification).

consolidation.summary:
BLOCK. All five protected-intent items hold on their own terms (engine diff empty, imperative-verbatim proven with a genuinely-failing negative control I independently reproduced by mutation, CLI-fallback table verified complete against an enumerated 18-verb list, settings.json never referenced, per-agent server identity confirmed via env-bound module state). Tests: 24/24 on the door's own suite, and the full suite's pinned red set (6) held exactly, no growth. Fowler pass: 12/12 smells rendered, 1 flagged (long-method on call_tool(), non-blocking observation), 0 unlogged overrides, rail exits 0.

The BLOCK is r7-delivery-path: the single foundational premise this whole gate's config-generation architecture rests on -- "project-scope .mcp.json cannot serve a cold/headless agent, it sits in Pending approval forever" -- does not reproduce. Independently re-ran the probe on Claude Code 2.1.226 against a genuinely cold project (zero prior ~/.claude.json state) and a real headless `claude -p` dispatch reached the door through the PLAIN project .mcp.json (no --mcp-config, no --strict-mcp-config) and got genuine engine output back, verified via server-side artifacts (mcp_calls.jsonl growth, mcp_server_started), not just the model's transcript. Isolated the actual friction the Commander likely hit: the ordinary per-tool permission gate every tool has in headless mode without --allowedTools -- not an MCP-specific approval gate, and identical friction on BOTH the plain-.mcp.json path and the per-dispatch-config path. Full detail, repro commands and scoped-null boundaries are in r7-delivery-path's recorded finding.
